clue.text: An awful cost 19 21 23 paradoxically settles?

definitions.meaning: a dreadful price or reckoning to be faced for something done
the wages of sin, read the wrong way round, are what one pays: rather than wages being paid to you, the sinner pays them in hell, so the phrase settles accounts

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a terrible price must follow when the wages of sin, oddly, come due.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half points at the linked answer at 19: wages are normally received, but the wages of sin are 'paid' in hell, hence the paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes serious trouble or a severe penalty awaiting someone.

clue.text: Core planet where the last shall be first

indicators.text: where the last shall be first
indicators.note: the biblical phrase tells us the final letter of the planet's name moves round to the front

parts.note: our planet is Earth

explanation.surface: A biblical promise of reversal applied to the centre of a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where the last shall be first' quotes Matthew and takes the final H of EARTH to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the heart of something is its central, most important part.

clue.text: Female monkey in meadow

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
the titi is a small South American monkey

clue.text: Worm wants red meat to become rotten

indicators.note: meat going rotten breaks down, so these letters decompose and reform

clue.text: Journal with influence that keeps work down

weight means influence or clout, as in carrying weight

explanation.definitionFit: Description: a heavy object on a desk stops papers, one's work, blowing away.

clue.text: Old solvers start to panic — that's right

parts.note: ye is the old form of 'you', the solvers being addressed

indicators.note: start to points at the opening letter of the word panic

clue.text: Arrangement has TV in higher place

parts.note: a television is a TV set
up means raised to a higher position

explanation.surface: A room layout puts the television somewhere high up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a setup is the way things are organised or arranged.

clue.text: Playboy playwright to tell in verse that's heard

indicators.note: that's heard says we want a word sounding like the verb rather than its spelling

parts.note: to sing is to tell a story in verse, as poets sing of heroes

explanation.surface: A playboy dramatist recounts things in rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: J M Synge wrote The Playboy of the Western World, so 'Playboy' names his play, not a lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Irish dramatist is best known for that play.

clue.text: Flow easily shifting oil produces capital

parts.note: words trip off the tongue when they flow easily

indicators.note: shifting moves the letters of oil into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil moving smoothly brings in money, a commodity-trade picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' turns OIL into OLI; 'capital' is a city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Shark pair snatches old dog

parts.note: the beagle is a hunting dog

explanation.definitionFit: Example: the porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Port or schnapps essentially brought round by twit

indicators.note: brought round turns those central letters back to front
essentially takes the core, the middle letters, of schnapps

parts.note: a twerp is a silly person, a twit

explanation.surface: A fool passes round drinks: port or schnapps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the heart of schnapps and 'brought round' turns it about. 'Port' looks like a drink beside schnapps but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport.

clue.text: Musical rook, on piano, in basket

indicators.note: on means the piano letter is placed in front of the musical, sitting on it in the clue's picture

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
Annie is a famous stage musical
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A tuneful crow perched on a piano, nestled in a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pannier is a basket, especially one carried by a pack animal or bike.

clue.text: Swimmer takes part in elite training

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tetra is a small tropical fish, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Supporter free European's held back for example

parts.note: to rid is to free
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the example abbreviation round, and 'held' lodges it inside the free and European words.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a ridgepole is the horizontal beam supporting the top of a roof or tent.

clue.text: Cancel FT to save capital? That's destructive

parts.note: to delete is to cancel

explanation.surface: Scrapping the FT to rescue money would be ruinous.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Rio as a former capital, and FT standing for 'us' the paper's own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something deleterious is harmful or damaging.

clue.text: Drink from nipple endlessly

clue.text: Time at private hotel and river residence

H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.definitionFit: Example: a townhouse is a house in a town, a type of home.

clue.text: Having too much on bad for an evil god sacrificing female

indicators.note: bad says these letters are spoiled and rearranged
sacrificing means giving up the female letter from the words that follow bad

explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing' removes the F of 'for' from FORANEVILGOD, then 'bad' rearranges ORANEVILGOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: overloading means burdening something with more than it can bear.

clue.text: 25 fools in society make killers

indicators.note: 25 down is the number two, so the fool word is used twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A couple of idiots in society turn out to be murderers.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to the answer at 25 down, TWO, so ASS appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: assassins are murderers, especially of public figures.

clue.text: Scots town's bustling estate to incorporate good little entrances

parts.note: Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

indicators.note: to incorporate means the rearranged estate takes the good letter inside
bustling stirs the letters of estate into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wicket-gates are small doors or gates, often set in larger ones.

clue.text: California Tales about one measure of heat

explanation.definitionFit: Unit: a calorie is a unit of heat energy.

clue.text: Whose feasting may lead to death?

definitions.text: Whose feasting may lead to death?

parts.words: Whose feasting may lead to death?

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase completes 'the wages of sin is death', from Paul's letter to the Romans.

clue.text: Ice-cream — there's a lot put into doughnuts

tons means a lot, so a ton is a great quantity

clue.text: Something blessed new hero staying fifty years by temple

indicators.note: staying means holding up or supporting, so the reshaped hero holds the other letters inside it
new means the letters of hero are refashioned

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.walkthrough: 'staying' is used in the sense of propping up or holding, so the rearranged hero (from 'new') wraps around fifty, years and temple.
